[SNIPPET -- cited in Sugiyama et al. arXiv:1407.0316, which was READ, and in the CRAN MHTdiscrete manual; Tarone itself NOT opened.] Extended to enumeration by Terada et al., PNAS 2013 (LAMP) [SNIPPET]. _the_one_transferable_asset: Cysteine chemistry. als_approach.py (the Cys6 approach to the Cys57-Cys146 disulfide, with its ~31 kcal/mol disease-timescale bound) and chalcogen_exchange.py (six S/Se thiol-disulfide exchange variants on disk) compute thiol chemistry and need NO fibril structure.
_the_arithmetic_that_blocks_it_first: The DISC1 cysteine motif is C680, C682, C684. The construct reported to form fibrils is 691-836, with the beta-core at 716-761. 680, 682 and 684 are all LESS THAN 691, so the triad sits outside the fibril-forming construct entirely -- not merely outside its core. Before any cysteine machinery is pointed at DISC1, somebody must establish whether those residues are anywhere near the aggregating region. This is arithmetic on the synthesis's own numbers and it is the first thing to check.
_a_correction_recorded_here_so_it_is_not: The synthesis closes by suggesting 'electronic structure of metal sites in SOD1' fits 'your existing SOD1 book and FPGA disease study'. Three separate strands are joined there that are not joined on disk: pd_copper_site_exposure.py computes SOLVENT ACCESSIBILITY (Shrake-Rupley), not electronic structure, under a PARKINSON'S hypothesis (Rowlands, copper-deficient histidine oxidation) rather than ALS aggregation; the FPGA/VQE pipeline is on 5-fluorouracil / thymidylate synthase and formamide, and SOD1 appears nowhere in it; and the 'SOD1 book' is the steric-zipper work on segments 30-35 and 147-153. In a grant or a paper that sentence would be wrong.

entries.claim_as_cited: FoldAmyloid is one of the four legacy predictors that failed on TRIOBP-1 in Bradshaw et al. 2017, and its server is unreachable, so half the legacy baseline cannot be re-run.
entries.action: READ IN FULL 15 Nov 2026, and it splits into two claims that must not be stated as one. (1) THE SERVER IS GONE. The paper publishes http://antares.protres.ru/fold-amyloid/ -- NOT the bioinfo.protres.ru host this project checked. Both return 000 over http and https, as does the amyloid_base.html dataset page. Dead or blocked from this host is still undecided. (2) THE METHOD IS NOT GONE. It is fully specified: three 20-value amino-acid scales (expected packing density; backbone-backbone H-bond probability by donor; the same by acceptor), sliding window 5 residues, a region called amyloidogenic when at least 5 consecutive residues exceed the cutoff, cutoffs 21.4 contacts/residue, 0.697 donor, 0.671 acceptor, 0.090 twice-hybrid and 0.062 triple-hybrid, and hybrids built by z-normalising each scale to mean 0 and sd 1 then averaging with equal weights. The ONLY missing piece is the 20 numeric values per scale: Figure 1 plots them as bar charts and the text refers the contact scale to Galzitskaya et al. 2006a. So FoldAmyloid is reimplementable, and the legacy baseline is three-of-four runnable rather than two-of-four.

entries.note: THREE THINGS THAT DEVALUE A FOLDAMYLOID NEGATIVE, all READ from the paper. (a) IT MISSES VQIVYK. 'In the case of unstructured tau-protein, only contact scale finds the experimentally detected (von Bergen et al., 2000) region (306-311)' -- two of three scales miss the canonical steric zipper. The abstract's '10 out of 11' is reached twice by different routes: the packing-density scale gets 10/11 missing a myoglobin fragment, and the acceptor scale -- the best performer on peptides -- gets 10/11 by missing tau PHF6. No single scale reaches 11. (b) THE DECISION UNIT IS FIVE RESIDUES: window 5, reliable frame 5, call on 5 consecutive residues above cutoff. This is primary-source support for the project's spine, that a negative call on a 25-residue proline- and charge-rich turn is uninformative by construction. (c) THE TAXONOMY HAS NO CATEGORY FOR OUR REGIONS. The paper names type I (hydrophobic) and type II (Gln/Asn-rich, GNNQQNY), states that 'most methods of prediction of amyloidogenic fragments are designed for searching for the regions of type I', and that 'our database contains no amyloidogenic peptides of the second type'. A proline- and charge-rich region is neither type.
entries.CONTAMINATION_2026_11_15: THE TRAINING SET IS NOW CHARACTERISED, closing a gap recorded in psychiatric_crossbeta_survey.md. 407 peptides, 144 amyloidogenic and 263 non-amyloidogenic, merged from Fernandez-Escamilla et al. 2004 (TANGO's OWN paper) and Thompson et al. 2006 (AmylHex, the 3D-profile paper). entries.note: FOUR USES. (a) THE CO-OCCURRENCE/INTERACTION DISTINCTION, now citable from the neurodegeneration field. This is exactly the Q5 finding in triobp_crmp1_npas3_dysbindin.md, reached independently. Seed amplification assays and RT-QuIC are clinical-grade in this field -- CSF SAA in a longitudinal AD cohort (Franzmeier 2025), alpha-syn RT-QuIC as a differential diagnostic (Quadalti 2021), Tau biosensor seeding on brain extracts (Tome 2023) -- and have never been pointed at psychiatric tissue. (d) POSITIONING. A 2026 comprehensive review of protein co-aggregation with over 300 references cites ZERO psychiatric co-aggregation work. _the_flagship_study_is_a_different_one: Nucifora et al., Am J Psychiatry (2019): 42 schizophrenia against 41 controls, prefrontal cortex and superior temporal gyrus, three brain banks, cold sarkosyl fractionation, mass spectrometry on the insoluble pellet; 20 of 42 cases carried elevated insoluble and ubiquitinated protein. The MS is reported AT PATHWAY LEVEL ONLY -- no named protein list, no fold changes, no FDR were found. Full text not retrievable (cookie wall, 403, paywall), so even the 42/41/20 counts are second-hand. This supplement is the highest-value outstanding retrieval in the whole group.
_the_strongest_contrast_has_no_published: Zaharija et al., IJMS 23(19):11048 (2022): insoluble TRIOBP-1 in 12 of 25 schizophrenia, 15 of 25 major depression, 2 of 50 controls, anterior cingulate. Called significant with NO p-value published for the headline comparison. Computed here from those counts: schizophrenia against control, Fisher exact p = 1.2e-05, odds ratio 18.0 (95% CI 4.1 to 79.4); depression against control, p = 1.4e-07, odds ratio 28.6 (95% CI 6.4 to 127.5). Those are strong, and they are the best case-control contrast in this literature -- but the counts are second-hand and the paper also prints an impossible p-value, '3.7 x 10^4', evidently a typo. Verify the counts against the PDF before any use.
_the_measurement_that_changes_the_framin: RETRACTED AS SOURCED, 16 Nov 2026. The claim was: aggregates from patient brain do NOT stimulate thioflavin T while recombinant DISC1 C-region fibrils do -- read as a statement inside Cukkemane 2025 attributing it to Leliveld 2009 and Korth 2012. BOTH LELIVELD PAPERS HAVE NOW BEEN READ IN FULL AND NEITHER CONTAINS A THIOFLAVIN T EXPERIMENT (see keys leliveld2008 and leliveld2009biochem). The attribution is wrong at least in half. It rests on Korth 2012 alone, still unread, or it is a mis-citation. NOT LOAD-BEARING, and now not even sourced. WHAT SURVIVES IS STRONGER: Leliveld 2008 reaches the same conclusion by circular dichroism. The rDISC598 dimer has 'essentially the same far-UV circular dichroism spectrum as the combined oligomer plus multimer fraction, indicating that rDISC598 self-associates as FOLDED SUBUNITS', and its Discussion states the group does 'not think that the type of Sarkosyl-resistant DISC1 aggregates described here are directly comparable with those found in classic misfolding diseases, because we do not have evidence of extensive conformational misfolding of multimeric DISC1'. A dye negative in a dilute extract can be a sensitivity failure; CD on purified protein cannot. CITE THE CD, NOT THE DYE. The honest statement stands: the patient-tissue species is not established to be an ordered amyloid, and no coordinate-based method can be validated against tissue.
_what_has_never_been_tried: No seeding assay has ever been run on psychiatric brain homogenate, although FRET biosensor and RT-QuIC assays are routine on post-mortem tissue in tau and alpha-synuclein. There is no published negative either, so 'not seeding-competent' and 'never tested' are currently indistinguishable. Cheap to answer and nobody has.
_the_arithmetic_that_blocks_it_first_IS_: The arithmetic holds: C680, C682 and C684 do lie outside the 691-836 fibril-forming construct, confirmed against the UniProt sequence (678-690 = KLCSCKCPLLGKV). The CONCLUSION drawn from it does not. The construct is NOT cysteine-free -- it carries C698, C762 and C782, and C762 sits immediately downstream of the reported beta-core boundary at 761. So a cysteine question inside the aggregating region does exist. What does not exist is any evidence for it: no source tests disulfide formation in DISC1, no source implicates oxidative conditions in its aggregation, both Cukkemane papers used no reducing agent and never mention disulfides, and the triad's only characterised function is arsenous-acid chelation through FREE thiols, which argues against disulfide bonding. 9RUX models the homologous mouse cluster with no disulfide, but the triad is not conserved in mouse (C-x-C, not C-x-C-x-C), so that structure cannot settle it either.
_the_core_range_is_contested_by_a_second: bioRxiv 10.1101/2023.08.03.551216 reports that NO single D, I, S or C region of DISC1 aggregates on its own in cells, and localises aggregation instead to a roughly 30-residue CENTRAL D-I LINKER, explicitly contrasting this with the C-terminal in vitro result. Both groups acknowledge the conflict. Note the shape of it: the TRIOBP-1 aggregation-critical region is likewise a 25-residue LINKER between the first two coiled coils, and was likewise missed by every predictor. Two coiled-coil scaffold proteins, two inter-domain linkers, two prediction failures -- that is a hypothesis with two independent points, and it is testable by a benchmark without any structure at all.
_the_one_computable_question_2026_11_15: Do the human-conserved triad thiols C682/C684 support disulfide formation or oxidation, and at what energetic cost? Input is PDB 9RUX (released 2026-05-06; Zhou et al., Nat Commun 2026), a 3.9 A cryo-EM homotetramer of MOUSE Disc1 322-722 that resolves the counterparts of human C682 and C684 at 6.70-8.10 A SG-SG. Cluster sizes measured from the coordinates: 618 atoms at 12 A, 754 at 14 A, inside the budget. It has wet-lab validation to be falsified against -- Watanabe et al. 2023 (Front Mol Biosci) show As(OH)3 binds the C-X-C-X-C motif with ALL THREE cysteines required, binding capacity 95+/-6% for wild type against 17+/-4% for the triple C->S mutant, which is the classical assay for clustered, reduced, accessible thiols. And NO quantum-chemical thiol-disulfide, cysteine-oxidation or disulfide-stability calculation exists for DISC1 or for ANY psychiatric-associated protein, at any level of theory: three structured queries returned only materials science, surface chemistry and non-psychiatric biology. The route is unoccupied.
_what_that_computable_question_does_NOT_: Two limits that must travel with it. FIRST, it is chemistry on the FOLDED protein, not on an aggregate interface: the triad sits outside both the 691-836 fibril construct and the reported 716-761 beta-core. That is the same distinction as tau PHF6 against the real Alzheimer interface, and it must be stated rather than blurred. SECOND, it does not explain the motivating phenotype: the ~200-230 kDa dopamine-induced high-molecular-weight DISC1 band, the only dopamine-dependent species ever measured, appears on gels whose stated sample buffers contain 8% beta-mercaptoethanol, so it is probably not disulfide-linked at all. Honest framing: a computable redox-switch question on a folded deposited domain, not a computation of psychiatric aggregation.
_S704C_is_closed_for_redox: Measured from 9RUX coordinates, not inferred. The mouse equivalent S701 is resolved in all four chains and is buried -- 96 neighbour heavy atoms within 8 A, contacting W393 and L349 -- and there is NO cysteine SG within 11.76 A of it in any chain. Both conditions for a redox role fail: not exposed, and no reachable partner. S704C is a folding and packing variant. Do not spend CPU on it.
_a_species_artefact_that_would_have_look: 9RUX's prettiest feature is mouse-only. Mouse C668 and C695 sit at 3.81-4.08 A SG-SG, reproduced across all four chains -- a textbook reduced near-disulfide about 1.8 A from bonding. Mouse C668 corresponds to human Y671, so the pair DOES NOT EXIST in human DISC1. Computing it would be mouse biology presented as human disease. Related brake: side-chain B-factors at these cysteines are 105-116 at 3.9 A, so the SG positions are modelled rather than observed and carry angstrom-scale uncertainty against a 2.05 A target bond. Any calculation must SCAN the SG-SG coordinate rather than trust the deposited geometry. And the protein was purified in 1 mM DTT at every step, so the structure says nothing about cellular redox state.
_the_uncontrolled_variable_nobody_has_ch: The 691-836 fibril construct contains three free cysteines (C698, C762, C782), and across Cukkemane 2021, Cukkemane 2025 and Zhou 2026 there is ZERO mention of DTT, TCEP, mercaptoethanol, reducing conditions, disulfide or redox. Those fibrils were therefore grown from a three-cysteine construct in air with the thiol oxidation state uncontrolled and unreported. Non-reducing against reducing SDS-PAGE would settle it in an afternoon and nobody has run it. This is a WET-LAB question, not a computation -- and it is the kind of specific, cheap, decisive question worth putting to an experimental group. Unverified for Narayanan 2011 (Europe PMC returned HTTP 500) and Leliveld 2009; established for the other three.

zaharija2024.WHY_THE_BLOCKER_STAYS_OPEN: Both abstracts say 'approximately 30 amino acids'. The actual claim is 384-415 = 32 residues, stated only in the preprint's Discussion and figures. AN ABSTRACT CANNOT DISCRIMINATE THE CASE WE ACTUALLY NEED TO EXCLUDE: the preprint's body text writes the deletion as delta-384-414 (31 residues) three times against delta-384-415 in its figures. If peer review resolved that slip the WRONG way -- or resolved it the right way and we never learn which -- the abstract reads identically either way. 'Approximately 30' is consistent with 31, 32 and 30 alike. The residual risk is precisely one residue at the C-terminal boundary, and only the full text or the figures can settle it.

zaharija2025thesis.citation: Zaharija B (2025). Investigating the Aggregation of DISC1 in Neuropsychiatric Disorders / Karakterizacija agregacije DISC1 proteina u neuropsihijatrijskim poremecajima. PhD thesis, University of Rijeka, Faculty of Biotechnology and Drug Development. Mentor N.J. Bradshaw, co-mentor R. Andretic Waldowski. Defended 23 June 2025. 245 pp, 48 figures, 36 tables, 392 references. urn:nbn:hr:193:978729.
zaharija2025thesis.provenance: Obtained by the author from the University of Rijeka repository after the faculty PDF 404'd and the repository host returned 418 to scripts. In copyright.
zaharija2025thesis.VERDICT: FALSIFIES THE BROAD NOVELTY CLAIM AND CLEARS THE LAST FREEZE BLOCKER. Section 4.3.5 runs FIVE aggregation predictors on full-length DISC1. The narrow claim in PREREGISTRATION §5.2 -- no PLM predictor -- survives intact.
zaharija2025thesis.CRITICAL_1_PREDICTORS_WERE_RUN: Section 4.3.5 'Assessing the aggregating potential of the linker region using online prediction tools', Figures 40 (A-F) and 41, Methods 3.2.3.4, and Table 5 (servers with URLs). Tools: AGGRESCAN (2007), TANGO (2004), FoldAmyloid (2010), MetAmyl (2013), ANuPP (2021) -- 'six different algorithms'. Input: full-length human L variant DISC1, NP_061132.2 (RefSeq, NOT UniProt Q9NRI5 -- VERIFY THE FRAMES MATCH). Default parameters, 'after which a consensus was determined for each amino acid'. This is the retrospective legacy arm of our project, already executed.
zaharija2025thesis.CRITICAL_2_WHAT_SURVIVES: NO protein language model, NO AggreProt (2024), NO AggrescanAI (2026), no AlphaFold. PREREGISTRATION §5.2 states the claim as 'no PLM predictor has ever been run on DISC1 or TRIOBP-1' -- STILL TRUE. CLAUDE.md's question (do MODERN predictors recover what the 2004-2010 generation missed) is untouched. STATE.md's broader phrasing was wrong and is struck.
zaharija2025thesis.CRITICAL_3_THEIR_RESULT_SUPPORTS_THE_PRE: Four of five tools gave 'aggregation/amyloid formation hotspots dispersed throughout the entirety of the protein sequence' -- they did NOT single out the linker. Only ANuPP did, naming AA 387-395 and AA 400-415 as highest nucleation capacity. So: legacy generation missed it, one 2021 tool found it, reported by the mapping group itself. Better-sourced than our own starting point -- but it is THEIRS. Cite, do not rediscover.
zaharija2025thesis.CRITICAL_4_SCOPE_CAVEAT: This is the thesis. The 2023 preprint (read in full) does NOT contain §4.3.5, so it was added later or is thesis-only; whether the published 2024 paper has it is unknown. TRIOBP-1 appears still clean: no predictor runs on it here, and none in Zaharija 2022.
zaharija2025thesis.what_it_adds_5_FREEZE_BLOCKER_CLEARED: 384-415 is confirmed and the delta-384-414 ambiguity is settled. Table 11 names the actual plasmids: 'DISC1 (delta-384-415)', 'DISC1 (1-655 delta-384-415)', 'DISC1 (1-836 delta-384-415)'. Section 4.3.4 and Conclusion 3.1 both say AA 384-415 and 'the 32 AA'. The preprint's delta-384-414 was a typo. ONE MORE SLIP IN THE SAME DOCUMENT: Figure 48's caption says 'AA 383-415' where its own text says 384-415.
zaharija2025thesis.what_it_adds_6_SUFFICIENCY_CONFIRMED: Our construct caveat holds. 1-383 does not aggregate, 1-415 does (Fig 38); the linker 384-538 alone aggregates (Fig 35C); deletion abolishes aggregation in 1-854, 1-836 and 1-655 (Fig 39). 384-415 was NEVER expressed alone. Conclusion 3.1 uses necessity language ('deletion of this region results in complete abolishment').
zaharija2025thesis.what_it_adds_7_TRIOBP_SLIP: p.177 says the TRIOBP-1 aggregating region was narrowed 'from 24 to just 8 amino acids'. 324-348 is 25 residues, not 24. Consistent with EIGHT for the minimal region.
zaharija2025thesis.what_it_adds_8_SECOND_AGGREGATION_MECHAN: I+S+C (539-854) aggregates while I+S (539-738) and S+C (635-836) do not. With Cukkemane's C-region beta-core this gives DISC1 two distinct aggregation routes, central and C-terminal. Also: the I region is NOT a stable domain in mammalian cells, contradicting the ESPRIT assignment -- relevant if any I-region row is ever considered.

mizuguchi2019.citation: Mizuguchi C, Nakagawa M, Namba N, Sakai M, Kurimitsu N, Suzuki A, Fujita K, Horiuchi S, Baba T, Ohgita T, Nishitsuji K, Saito H (2019). Mechanisms of aggregation and fibril formation of the amyloidogenic N-terminal fragment of apolipoprotein A-I. J Biol Chem 294(36):13515-13524. doi:10.1074/jbc.RA119.008000
mizuguchi2019.VERDICT: CIRCULAR. SUPPLIES NO CLEAN ROW. Read because it was the best lead from the first validation-set sweep; reading reversed the verdict. All four deletion variants were designed to remove segments that AmylPred2 and Zyggregator had ranked -- and AMYLPRED2 IS IN THIS PROJECT'S OWN LEGACY PREDICTOR SET.
mizuguchi2019.why_the_snippet_was_misleading: The abstract says 'using a series of deletion variants', which reads as unbiased mapping. The construct design is in the Introduction and Figure 1B, not the abstract. General lesson: abstracts describe the assay and bury the construct design, so snippet-level found_by assessment is biased TOWARDS FALSE CLEAN.
mizuguchi2019.the_science_which_is_sound: 14-22 is necessary: no ThT rise, no coil-to-beta transition by CD, no fibrils by AFM or TEM (small spherical aggregates instead), reduced cytotoxicity in HEK293. 32-40 and 50-58 are not necessary but slow nucleation and growth. 50-58 entropically drives nucleation -- activation entropy of nucleation flips from +55 to -281 J/mol/K on deletion. 68-76 enthalpically INHIBITS fibril growth, so deleting it raises ThT. Pyrene excimer puts 22 and 52 in contact and excludes positions 2, 8, 36, 72, 81 from the core.
mizuguchi2019.construct: apoA-I 1-83/G26R: a disease-variant N-terminal fragment, expressed in E. coli as a thioredoxin fusion, thrombin-cleaved leaving two extra residues (Gly-Ser) at the N terminus. NOT full-length wild type. Lipid-bound behaviour differs from solution (Fig S9).
mizuguchi2019.the_one_legitimate_use: Circularity is TOOL-SPECIFIC. AmylPred2 and Zyggregator chose the region; AggreProt, AggrescanAI and the PLMs did not. apoA-I 14-22 could therefore be a labelled POSITIVE CONTROL for the modern arm only. It cannot test the central hypothesis: a region picked because legacy tools ranked it top is predictable by construction, so scoring modern tools on it measures agreement with legacy, not recovery of what experiment found.
mizuguchi2019.incidental: p.13521 writes 'delta-68-78' twice where Table 1, Results and Methods all say delta-68-76. Seventh residue-number slip found by reading primaries and the FIRST FROM OUTSIDE THE BRADSHAW GROUP.

bradshawkorth2018.citation: Bradshaw NJ & Korth C (2018). Protein misassembly and aggregation as potential convergence points for non-genetic causes of chronic mental illness. Mol Psychiatry 24:936-951. doi:10.1038/s41380-018-0133-2.
bradshawkorth2018.provenance: READ IN FULL, 16 Nov 2026, publisher PDF supplied by the author. Springer Nature.
bradshawkorth2018.IT_IS_A_REVIEW: A Perspective, not a primary. CLAUDE.md forbids taking residue numbers from a review, so nothing here promotes a row. Its two arithmetic claims were checked anyway and both hold: TRIOBP-1 324-348 is 25 residues, matching 'just 25 amino acids'; NPAS3 211-331 is 121, matching 'a 121-amino acid-long central region'.
bradshawkorth2018.WHAT_IT_IS_ACTUALLY_FOR: IT PINS THE CITATION OF THE NEVER-OPENED PRIMARY. Two rows in regions.json name 'Bradshaw et al. 2017' as their source and carry source_version = source_not_opened, with no fuller citation anywhere in the project. Reference 110 of this review gives it exactly.
bradshawkorth2018.THE_2017_PRIMARY: Bradshaw NJ, Yerabham ASK, Marreiros R, Zhang T, Nagel-Steger L, Korth C (2017). An UNPREDICTED aggregation-critical region of the actin-polymerizing protein TRIOBP-1/Tara, determined by elucidation of its domain structure. J Biol Chem 292:9583-9598. NOTE THE TITLE: the word 'unpredicted' is in it. The predictor-failure claim that this whole project treats as cited evidence is the TITLE of the paper nobody here has opened.
bradshawkorth2018.what_it_corroborates_at_review_grade: Table 2 gives the TRIOBP aggregation-critical domain as '324-348 [110]', attributing it to that 2017 JBC paper, and the text restates it as 'mapped to just 25 amino acids' on 'a loop between two predicted coiled coils'. Consistent with our row's range and with its attribution. REVIEW GRADE ONLY -- it does not substitute for opening the primary.
bradshawkorth2018.THE_THIOFLAVIN_T_TRAIL_IS_CORRECTED_AGAI: reports/PDFs_to_obtain.md says the ThT claim 'now rests on Korth 2012 alone'. THIS REVIEW POINTS SOMEWHERE ELSE ENTIRELY: 'aggregates of DISC1 (but not yet the other proteins) have been tested with dyes associated with classic amyloid-based aggregation (thioflavin T and thioflavin S), yielding POTENTIALLY CONTRADICTORY RESULTS IN DIFFERENT EXPRESSION SYSTEMS [62, 82]', where 62 = Tanaka 2017 (J Clin Invest 127:1438) and 82 = Trossbach 2016 (Mol Psychiatry 21:1561). Korth 2012 is reference 9 of this review and is cited for 'DISC1opathies', NOT for ThT. SECOND INDEPENDENT POINTER AWAY FROM KORTH 2012 -- Cukkemane 2021 also sourced the ThT-positive claim to Tanaka 2017. The honest statement is that the ThT evidence is CONTRADICTORY BETWEEN EXPRESSION SYSTEMS and traces to Tanaka 2017 and Trossbach 2016.

two_review_grade_leads_not_promoted.NPAS3_211-331: Table 2 gives an aggregation-critical region of 211-331 for NPAS3 V304I, citing Nucifora 2016 (Mol Neuropsychiatry 2:133). 121 residues, verified. NPAS3 is on the project's psychiatric candidate list. A POSSIBLE ROW, but the primary must be opened first and the region is very broad -- 121 residues is a domain, not a motif.
two_review_grade_leads_not_promoted.CRMP1_1-127_IS_NOT_A_MAPPED_REGION: Table 2 gives '1-127*' for CRMP1lv, and the asterisk is defined as 'Implied as only region unique to the long variant, lv'. THE PAPER STATES IT IS AN INFERENCE FROM ISOFORM DIFFERENCE, NOT A MAPPING. It must never be entered as an experimentally mapped region. A good example of why the table footnote matters as much as the table.

bradshawkorth2018.a_statement_worth_keeping: 'While visible deposits of aggregated protein have not yet been detected in CMI patients, we propose the existence of more subtle protein misassembly in these conditions.' The authors are explicit that the visible-deposit evidence is absent. Consistent with Cukkemane 2021's 'DISC1 amyloid has not been reported either in human post-mortem brains or in animal models'.

bradshaw2014.citation: Bradshaw NJ, Bader V, Prikulis I, Lueking A, Mullner S, Korth C (2014). Aggregation of the Protein TRIOBP-1 and Its Potential Relevance to Schizophrenia. PLoS ONE 9(10):e111196. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0111196.
bradshaw2014.provenance: READ IN FULL, 16 Nov 2026, publisher PDF supplied by the author. PLoS ONE, CC BY, so the publisher PDF is the version of record.
bradshaw2014.VERDICT: THIS IS WHERE THE LEGACY-ARM PREDICTOR RUN ON TRIOBP-1 LIVES, and it is specified well enough to reproduce. All four tools of PREREGISTRATION 5.1 with thresholds and URLs, plus an explicit consensus rule. It also contains a documented FALSE POSITIVE of that arm, experimentally refuted in the same paper.
bradshaw2014.what_it_does_NOT_contain: NO mapping of 324-348. That is the 2017 paper. This 2014 paper establishes that TRIOBP-1 aggregates, that TRIOBP-4 does not, that aggregation rises in post-mitotic cells, and that the PH domain is not responsible. The 25-aa region is not identified here.
bradshaw2014.the_frame_is_not_stated: No accession and no reading frame for the analysed sequence. The 652-aa frame was introduced in 2017. Resolve before any attempt to reproduce the 2014 run.

samardzija2026.citation: Samardzija B, Renner E, Palkovits M, Bradshaw NJ (2026). Levels of aggregation of proteins related to mental illness, assayed by insolubility, vary across the brains of individuals. Sci Rep 16:8240. doi:10.1038/s41598-026-35767-0. Received 20 Oct 2025, accepted 8 Jan 2026, published 11 Feb 2026. CC BY-NC-ND.
samardzija2026.provenance: READ IN FULL, 16 Nov 2026, publisher PDF supplied by the author.
samardzija2026.VERDICT: NO PREDICTOR RUNS AND NO NEW MAPPED REGIONS. It adds no row. Its value is three-fold: it is the group's MOST RECENT paper and still contains no aggregation prediction of any kind, so the 5.2 novelty claim survives another check; it moves the controls caveat from a thesis into a peer-reviewed journal; and it corroborates the DISC1 384-415 row from a third paper.
samardzija2026.NOVELTY_CLAIM_SURVIVES: Named software is ImageLab (Bio-Rad) only. No TANGO, AGGRESCAN, FoldAmyloid, ProA, WALTZ, PASTA, AmylPred2, ZipperDB, AggreProt, AggrescanAI or any protein language model. This is the newest output of the group that mapped both of the project's founding regions, and the gap holds.
samardzija2026.IT_CORROBORATES_DISC1_384_415_FROM_A_THI: Methods, antibody verification: 'plasmids encoding full length 854-amino acid long human DISC1, or only amino acids 257-655 of human DISC1, representing the D and I domains, AS WELL AS THE AGGREGATION PRONE-REGION BETWEEN THEM [44]', where reference 44 IS Zaharija & Bradshaw 2024, the unobtainable version of record. VERIFIED ARITHMETICALLY: with D at 257-383 and I at 539-655 (the ESPRIT list in Cukkemane 2021), our row 384-415 lies strictly between D and I and inside the 257-655 construct. BOTH CHECKS PASS. This is citing-paper grade, not a boundary statement -- it does NOT resolve delta-384-414 versus delta-384-415 -- but it is a third independent document placing the region where our row puts it.
samardzija2026.THE_CONTROLS_CAVEAT_IS_NOW_PEER_REVIEWED: STATE.md already forbids calling these 'the schizophrenia aggregates', on the strength of the 2025 thesis. That caveat is now published: 'Five of the eight controls also showed some protein insolubility of these proteins'; 'most proteins could be found, to some extent, to be insoluble across various groups of individuals, including those that had no psychiatric diagnosis'; and the authors state flatly that 'the mere presence of insoluble protein cannot be used for diagnostic reference'. CITE THIS RATHER THAN THE THESIS.
samardzija2026.a_caveat_on_the_premise_not_on_our_rows: The paper's central finding is that insolubility is HETEROGENEOUS ACROSS BRAIN REGIONS WITHIN ONE INDIVIDUAL, and even between hemispheres -- in patient R 'the left hemisphere showed most insoluble DISC1 in the dorsal premotor cortex and temporal cortex, while the right showed most in the fusiform gyrus and parietal cortex'. It concludes that single-region studies may UNDERESTIMATE prevalence. This bears on the post-mortem evidence that motivates the field, NOT on this project's rows, which come from fragment-level mapping in cells and recombinant protein. Do not conflate the two kinds of evidence.
samardzija2026.no_statistics: 'Statistical analysis was not performed, due to the low number of samples in any individual test.' The insolubility threshold is explicitly exploratory: 'at least 1.5-fold higher than the mean'. Treat all of its quantitative statements as descriptive.

venko2026.citation: Venko K & Zerovnik E (2026). Assessment of Aggregation- and Condensation-Prone Regions of Proteins Involved in Neurodegenerative, Neurological and Mental-State Diseases. Biomolecules 16:1286. doi:10.3390/biom16091286. Received 30 Jun 2026, accepted 3 Sep 2026, published 5 Sep 2026. CC BY. ARIS grants P1-0017, P1-0140.
venko2026.provenance: READ IN FULL, 18 Nov 2026, publisher PDF supplied by the author. An earlier abstract-only read was recorded as unresolved because Europe PMC returned 503 on the full text.
venko2026.VERDICT: DOES NOT PRE-EMPT THIS PROJECT, AND MUST BE CITED. It is the closest published neighbour -- 20 aggregating proteins including DISC1, TRIOBP1, FUS, tau, hnRNPA1 and alpha-synuclein, run through >40 predictors -- but it reports PREDICTOR OUTPUT, not a benchmark. There is no statistic, no null model, no decoy construction, no pre-registration, no success threshold, no error bar and no validation set. Agreement with experiment is assessed narratively, protein by protein, in prose.
venko2026.THE_AUTHORS_STATE_THE_GAP_THEMSELVES: Verbatim, Discussion: 'A major limitation of the present study is the lack of experimental evidence for the investigated proteins, which prevents a direct validation of the predicted CPRs and APRs.' And Results: 'only a subset of these regions has thus far been experimentally characterized.' The thing they say they lack is exactly what data/regions.json is.
venko2026.WHAT_IT_GIVES_THIS_PROJECT: 1. A PUBLISHED NEGATIVE ON TRIOBP-1 324-348, from a consensus panel: 'Unexpectedly, this region was only predicted by FuzzDrop in our analysis, whereas several other regions of TRIOBP1 received stronger computational support to be capable of inducing aggregation.' 2. A SECOND published negative, on DISC1 716-761: 'The DISC1 C-region can form amyloid-like fibers in vitro at residues 716-761, which surprisingly are not defined in our computational studies.' 3. It cites Zaharija & Bradshaw 2024 (its ref [122]) as the source of the DISC1 central-region result -- a third document pointing at the paper still unread here.
venko2026.AND_ONE_RESULT_THAT_CUTS_AGAINST_US: For DISC1 384-415 the Venko consensus is NOT a miss. Their Table 3 places a >=2-predictor aggregation-prone region at 403-411 and >=4-predictor amyloid-prone regions at 388-394 and 400-406, all three strictly inside our row, in the same 854-residue frame. Recorded here because it weakens the 'the predictors miss it' framing for that row specifically, and the record should not quote only the half that helps.
venko2026.CORRECTION_TO_OUR_OWN_EARLIER_FRAMING: '44 programs' is the headline but NOT the denominator for regions. Only a subset return residue-level calls: by Table 2 that is 5 aggregation-region tools (SODA, FuzDrop, ANuPP, Aggrescan, TANGO), 14 amyloid, 5 condensation, 2 prion. So 'only FuzDrop predicted TRIOBP-1 324-348' is 1 of 5, not 1 of 44, and must be quoted that way.
venko2026.DEFECT_1_TRIOBP1_FRAME_COLLISION: Table 1 declares the TRIOBP1 sequence as '593 (1772-2365)' under Q9H2D6 -- the OLD 593-residue frame, which CLAUDE.md requires +59 to reach NP_008963.3. But the region they compare against, 324-348, is a 652-FRAME number (Bradshaw 2017 JBC, read in full here 16 Nov 2026). In the 593 frame that region is 265-289. Their predicted TRIOBP1 regions and the experimental region they test them against are therefore stated in two different frames, 59 residues apart, and the 'only FuzzDrop' comparison cannot be verified as written. NOT YET RAISED WITH THE AUTHORS.
venko2026.DEFECT_2_CITATION_SLIP: They attribute 324-348 to ref [123] = Bradshaw et al. 2014 PLoS ONE 9:e111196. Both papers were read in full here on 16 Nov 2026: the 2014 PLoS ONE paper points at the PH domain (our 60-189 row, which the deletion work did NOT support); 324-348 is from Bradshaw et al. 2017 JBC 292:9583, whose title is literally 'An unpredicted aggregation-critical region...'. The 2017 paper is not in their reference list at all.
venko2026.DEFECT_3_INTERNAL_INCONSISTENCY_ON_DISC1: The text says 716-761 is 'not defined in our computational studies'. That holds for their amyloid consensus (nearest calls 699-705 and 823-829, both outside) but NOT for their aggregation consensus, whose DISC1 row lists 751-757 -- inside 716-761. The published negative above is therefore true of 14 amyloid tools and false of their own 5-tool aggregation panel.
venko2026.WHAT_IT_DOES_NOT_CONTAIN: No m/M, no information limit, no floor, no calibration, no power statement, no per-row uncertainty of any kind. No CPAD or training-set membership check, so no circularity control. No construct column: regions are compared without regard to which construct established them. No found_by column, so prediction-discovered and experiment-discovered regions are compared side by side -- for TRIOBP1 their own narrative does exactly this, discussing the PH-domain prediction and the 324-348 experiment in one paragraph.
venko2026.CONSEQUENCE_FOR_THE_WRITE_UP: Cite as the state of the art in APPLYING predictors to this protein set, and as independent corroboration of the project's premise on two rows. The contrast to state is methodological, not territorial: they publish predictions for proteins whose regions are mostly unmapped; this project publishes mapped regions and a pre-registered test. Do NOT claim they failed to benchmark -- they did not attempt to, and they say so.
